Must.snippet: DATA-001 Priceable Entity The workspace must support the creation and management of Priceable Entities.
Supported Priceable Entity types must include, at minimum: ● product; ● SKU or product variant; ● service; ● another organisation-defined directly priceable offering.
Where individual SKUs or variants of a product have distinct selling prices, each independently priced SKU or variant must be represented as its own Priceable Entity.
Pricing dimensions such as location, region, channel, customer group, business unit, vendor or price list must remain distinct from the Priceable Entity itself.
Each Priceable Entity must have, at minimum: ● unique Owómidé identifier; ● organisation-defined name; ● entity type; ● status.
Currency must be associated with the applicable monetary record or pricing context rather than assumed to be an immutable property of the Priceable Entity.

The Priceable Entity model must remain sufficiently flexible to support organisations that price at product, SKU, variant or service level without requiring every organisation to use the same catalogue hierarchy.

Must Not.snippet: Categories and product groups must not become Priceable Entities solely because they are used to organise, filter or apply pricing work across multiple Priceable Entities.

May.snippet: A product may itself be a Priceable Entity where the organisation prices that product directly.

A Priceable Entity may therefore have different Price Records, Cost Records or pricing outcomes across supported pricing dimensions without becoming a different Priceable Entity unless the organisation's underlying commercial object is itself different.

Where available, a Priceable Entity may also contain: ● SKU, product code or external identifier; ● parent product or related organisational grouping; ● category; ● brand; ● base unit of measure; ● description; ● organisation-specific reference fields.

Must.snippet: DATA-003 Price Record and Current Price The system must allow an organisation to maintain structured Price Records for Priceable Entities.

Each Price Record must identify, where applicable: ● Priceable Entity; ● price amount; ● currency; ● applicable pricing dimensions; ● effective-from date or timestamp; ● effective-to date or timestamp where applicable; ● source; ● last updated timestamp.

The system must support different Price Records for the same Priceable Entity where pricing legitimately differs by location, channel, customer group, price list, currency or another configured pricing dimension.
The system must also preserve multiple Price Records over time for the same pricing context where the selling price changes.
A Current Price must therefore remain associated with: ● the Priceable Entity; ● price amount; ● currency; ● applicable pricing dimensions; ● effective context; ● source Price Record.

…ce Records prevent the Current Price from being determined unambiguously, the system must identify the Current Price as unresolved and require appropriate authorised correction or selection rather than silently choosing a value.
A historical Price Record must remain preserved after it ceases to be Current Price.
Where no applicable Price Record exists, Current Price must be represented as unavailable rather than assumed to be zero or inferred from another pricing context.
Any consequential pricing work that uses Current Price must remain traceable to the exact Price Record and pricing context from which that Current Price was determined.

Must Not.snippet: The system must not silently treat the newest Price Record, most recently imported value or another arbitrary Price Record as the Current Price where more than one record could apply.
For the same Priceable Entity and exact pricing context, the system must not represent conflicting Price Records as simultaneously being the Current Price for the same reference time.
A future-effective Price Record must not become Current Price before its applicable effective time.

requirements.title: Cost Record and Applicable Unit Cost

Must.snippet: DATA-004 Cost Record and Applicable Unit Cost Where cost information is available, the MVP must allow authorised users to maintain structured Cost Records for priceable entities.

Each Cost Record must identify, where applicable: ● affected priceable entity; ● cost amount; ● currency; ● unit of measure or cost unit; ● cost basis; ● applicable pricing dimensions; ● effective date or effective period; ● source; ● last updated timestamp.
Cost basis must identify what the cost value represents.
The MVP must allow more than one Cost Record to exist for the same priceable entity where the records represent different cost bases, pricing dimensions or effective periods.
For every deterministic pricing calculation that requires cost, the system must identify the Applicable Unit Cost used by that calculation.
The Applicable Unit Cost must be traceable to either: ● a structured Cost Record; or ● an explicit assumed cost permitted under the applicable assumption requirements.

The calculation context must preserve enough information to identify: ● cost amount used; ● cost basis used; ● currency; ● applicable unit of measure; ● applicable pricing dimensions; ● source Cost Record or explicit assumption; ● effective context relevant to…
…not be determined from the pricing context or organisation configuration, the system must require an authorised user to identify the applicable cost rather than selecting one silently.
Changes to cost information over time must create or preserve historical cost context rather than overwriting the cost basis used in earlier consequential pricing work.

Must Not.snippet: It must not be assumed to represent a universal accounting definition of cost.
Owómidé must not silently treat the newest Cost Record, an average historical cost or any particular cost basis as the correct cost for every pricing decision.
Where a cost cannot be expressed on a unit basis compatible with the selling price, the system must not use that value directly in gross-profit, gross-margin, markup or target-price calculations.

May.snippet: Supported cost bases may include: ● acquisition or purchase cost; ● landed cost; ● production or manufacturing cost; ● direct service-delivery cost; ● another organisation-defined cost basis.

Not Required.snippet: The MVP is not required to operate as a full cost-accounting system, perform enterprise-wide overhead allocation or independently construct accounting cost values from incomplete source data.

Must.snippet: ANALYSIS-006 Price Adjustment and Price Change Calculation Where a pricing action derives a proposed selling price from a baseline price, the baseline used by the calculation must be explicitly identifiable.
Where the baseline is Current Price, the calculation must use the Current Price defined in DATA-003 for the affected Priceable Entity and pricing context.
An authorised user may define another supported pricing baseline where the pricing action permits it, but that baseline must remain explicitly distinguishable from Current Price.
Where: Baseline Price = B Percentage Adjustment = R Absolute Adjustment = A the MVP must support the following deterministic calculations where applicable.

Where a promotional, markdown or other pricing action directly specifies the final selling price rather than an adjustment, that value must be treated as the proposed selling price rather than recalculated through an adjustment formula.
After the proposed selling price is determined, the system must calculate price change against Current Price where an unambiguous Current Price is available under DATA-003.
…t Price) / Current Price) × 100 Where Current Price is zero, percentage price change must be represented as unavailable rather than producing an undefined or misleading percentage.
Where Current Price is unavailable or unresolved, absolute and percentage change against Current Price must be represented as unavailable.

Where the product displays a change relative to an alternative pricing baseline, that result must be explicitly identified as change relative to that baseline and must not be labelled as change from Current Price.
The system must preserve the pricing action, baseline value, baseline type, adjustment value, calculation method and resulting proposed selling price used in the calculation.
Where Current Price is the baseline, the preserved calculation context must remain traceable to the exact source Price Record defined under DATA-003.

Must Not.snippet: Where no unambiguous Current Price exists, the system must not silently select another Price Record as Current Price.
…-value reduction: Proposed Selling Price = B - Discount Amount Percentage reductions must not be less than 0% or greater than 100%.
Absolute reductions must not produce a negative proposed selling price.

Unavailability of Current Price must not prevent a pricing action from being deterministically calculated where that action validly uses another explicitly identified pricing baseline and all inputs required for that calculation are available.

Where the product displays a change relative to an alternative pricing baseline, that result must be explicitly identified as change relative to that baseline and must not be labelled as change from Current Price.

May.snippet: The baseline may be the current selling price or another supported pricing baseline explicitly defined by the pricing action.
An authorised user may define another supported pricing baseline where the pricing action permits it, but that baseline must remain explicitly distinguishable from Current Price.

Where Pricing Proposal Version Validity is included, the exported value must use the canonical validity states defined in PROP-013: ● Current; ● Superseded; ● Expired.

Where execution information is included, it must be represented separately using the applicable execution states defined in EXEC-010: ● Not Started; ● In Progress; ● Partially Implemented; ● Implemented; ● Implementation Exception.

An Approved or Authorised Within Policy Proposal version that is Superseded or Expired must preserve both pieces of information rather than replacing its historical Proposal status with its current validity state.
Exported status information must remain consistent with the authoritative Proposal and execution records inside Owómidé.
